questions.question: Explain, using reflection and absorption, why a red apple looks red, a sheet of paper looks white and a piece of charcoal looks black in sunlight.
questions.expected_answer: Sunlight is white light, a mixture of all colours. An opaque object absorbs some colours and reflects others; its colour is the colour of the reflected light. The red apple absorbs most colours (orange, yellow, green, blue, violet) and reflects mainly red, so red light reaches the eye. White paper reflects all colours about equally, so the reflected light is white. Charcoal absorbs almost all colours and reflects very little light, so it looks black (black is the absence of reflected light).

questions.question: Explain how a red filter works. Predict and explain the appearance of a white shirt, a red cap and a green shirt in a room lit only by red light.
questions.expected_answer: A red filter transmits red light and absorbs the other colours; it removes colours, it does not add red. In red light, only red is available to reflect. White shirt: reflects all colours, so it reflects the red and looks red. Red cap: reflects red, so it looks red. Green shirt: reflects only green and absorbs red; there is no green to reflect, so it reflects almost nothing and looks black (very dark).

questions.question: Explain why dark surfaces become hotter in sunlight than light surfaces, give one use of each, and describe a fair test to investigate this.
questions.expected_answer: Absorbed light energy is transferred to the material as heat. Dark surfaces absorb more of the light falling on them (light surfaces reflect more), so they gain more energy and warm faster. Uses: black panels in solar water heaters and solar cookers absorb sunlight; white walls and roofs in hot regions reflect sunlight and keep buildings cool. Fair test: two identical cans with equal volumes of water at the same starting temperature, one black and one white, placed side by side in the sun; record water temperature every 5 minutes. Independent variable: surface colour; dependent: temperature; controlled: volume, starting temperature, can size and material, sunlight, time.
